That is the careful version,\n17\twritten by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a\n18\tconfidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.\n19\t\n20\tThe registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer\n21\tto implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —\n41\tit does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and\n42\tthere is no opt-out flag.\n43\t\n44\tUpdate `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.\n45\t\n46\t## Acceptance criteria\n47\t\n48\t- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's\n49\t      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; {result: response} : response;\n31\t}\n32\t\n33\texport type ToolDefinitionSource = ToolDefinition | (() => ToolDefinition);\n34\t\n35\texport interface RegisteredTool {\n36\t  definition: ToolDefinition;\n37\t  execute: ToolExecutor;\n38\t}\n39\t\n40\tinterface StoredTool {\n41\t  definitionSource: ToolDefinitionSource;\n42\t  execute: ToolExecutor;\n43\t  validators: WeakMap<object, ValidateFunction>;\n44\t}\n45\t\n46\t// A schema that ajv cannot compile is a programming error, not a runtime input problem: name the tool.\n47\tfunction compileValidator(toolName: string, schema: ToolDefinition['inputSchema']): ValidateFunction {\n48\t  try {\n49\t    return ajv.compile(schema);\n50\t  } catch (error) {\n51\t    const detail = error instanceof Error ? source() : source;\n61\t  }\n62\t\n63\t  register(definition: ToolDefinitionSource, execute: ToolExecutor): void {\n64\t    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(definition);\n65\t    const validators = new WeakMap<object, ValidateFunction>();\n66\t    validators.set(resolved.inputSchema, compileValidator(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema));\n67\t    this.tools.set(resolved.name, {definitionSource: definition, execute, validators});\n68\t  }\n69\t\n70\t  get(name: string): RegisteredTool | undefined {\n71\t    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n72\t    if (!tool) return undefined;\n73\t    return {definition: this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource), execute: tool.execute};\n74\t  }\n75\t\n76\t  getDefinitions(): ToolDefinition[] {\n77\t    return [...this.tools.values()].map(t => this.resolveDefinition(t.definitionSource));\n78\t  }\n79\t\n80\t  getPromptInstructions(): string[] {\n81\t    return this.getDefinitions()\n82\t      .filter(t => t.promptInstructions)\n83\t      .map(t => `${t.name}: ${t.promptInstructions}`);\n84\t  }\n85\t\n86\t  getExamplePrompts(): string[] {\n87\t    return this.getDefinitions().flatMap(t => t.examplePrompts ?? []);\n88\t  }\n89\t\n90\t  has(name: string): boolean {\n91\t    return this.tools.has(name);\n92\t  }\n93\t\n94\t  /** Validates input against the declared schema and returns a rejection response instead of throwing; see specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md. */\n95\t  async execute(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext): Promise<ToolResponse> {\n96\t    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n97\t    if (!tool) {\n98\t      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n99\t      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n100\t    }\n101\t    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource);\n102\t    let validate = tool.validators.get(resolved.inputSchema);\n103\t    if (!validate) {\n104\t      validate = compileValidator(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n105\t      tool.validators.set(resolved.inputSchema, validate);\n106\t    }\n107\t    if (!validate(input)) {\n108\t      const violations = (validate.errors ?? {result: response} : response;\n}\n\nexport type ToolDefinitionSource = ToolDefinition | (() => ToolDefinition);\n\nexport interface RegisteredTool {\n  definition: ToolDefinition;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n}\n\ninterface StoredTool {\n  definitionSource: ToolDefinitionSource;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n  validators: WeakMap<object, ValidateFunction>;\n}\n\n// A schema that ajv cannot compile is a programming error, not a runtime input problem: name the tool.\nfunction compileValidator(toolName: string, schema: ToolDefinition['inputSchema']): ValidateFunction {\n  try {\n    return ajv.compile(schema);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const detail = error instanceof Error ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2a20e4c274274b7f85a2941b","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tname: CI\n2\t\n3\ton:\n4\t  pull_request:\n5\t  push:\n6\t    branches: [main]\n7\t  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n8\t  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n9\t  workflow_dispatch:\n10\t  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n11\t  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n12\t  schedule:\n13\t    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n14\t\n15\t# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\n16\tpermissions:\n17\t  contents: read\n18\t\n19\t# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n20\t# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\n21\tconcurrency:\n22\t  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n23\t  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n24\t\n25\tjobs:\n26\t  verify:\n27\t    name: Verify\n28\t    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n29\t    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n30\t    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n31\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n32\t    steps:\n33\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n34\t        with:\n35\t          persist-credentials: false\n36\t          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n37\t          # it resolves cited content from\n38\t          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n39\t          fetch-depth: 0\n40\t\n41\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n42\t        with:\n43\t          node-version: '22'\n44\t          cache: npm\n45\t\n46\t      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n47\t      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n48\t      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n49\t      - name: Install\n50\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n51\t\n52\t      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n53\t      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n54\t      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n55\t      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n56\t      - name: Type check\n57\t        run: npm run typecheck\n58\t\n59\t      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n60\t      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n61\t      - name: Type check the example\n62\t        run: npm run typecheck:example\n63\t\n64\t      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n65\t        run: npm run eslint\n66\t\n67\t      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n68\t      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n69\t      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n70\t      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n71\t      # passing check should look like.\n72\t      #\n73\t      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n74\t      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n75\t      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n76\t      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n77\t      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n78\t      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n79\t      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n80\t        run: npm run lint:backlog\n81\t\n82\t      - name: Format check\n83\t        run: npm run prettier:check\n84\t\n85\t      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n86\t      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n87\t      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n88\t        run: npm run test:coverage\n89\t\n90\t      - name: Build\n91\t        run: npm run build\n92\t\n93\t      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n94\t      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n95\t      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n96\t      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n97\t      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n98\t      - name: Spec anchor check\n99\t        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n100\t\n101\t      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n102\t      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n103\t      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n104\t      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n105\t      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n106\t      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n107\t      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n108\t      - name: Documented code blocks\n109\t        run: npm run docs:check\n110\t\n111\t      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n112\t      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n113\t      - name: Documented paths resolve\n114\t        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n115\t\n116\t      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n117\t        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n118\t\n119\t      - name: Documented regions\n120\t        run: npm run check:regions\n121\t\n122\t      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n123\t      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n124\t      - name: Spec citations name their test\n125\t        run: npm run spec:names\n126\t\n127\t      - name: Spec link placement\n128\t        run: npm run check:spec-links\n129\t\n130\t      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n131\t      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n132\t      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n133\t      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n134\t      # and never gates.\n135\t      - name: Spec status\n136\t        run: npm run check:spec-status\n137\t\n138\t      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n139\t      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The\n140\t      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.\n141\t      - name: Changelog entry\n142\t        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')\n143\t        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes\n144\t        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step\n145\t        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private\n146\t        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.\n147\t        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh \"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}\"\n148\t\n149\t  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain\n150\t  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as\n151\t  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n152\t  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n153\t  build-chain:\n154\t    name: Build chain\n155\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n156\t    steps:\n157\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n158\t        with:\n159\t          persist-credentials: false\n160\t\n161\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n162\t        with:\n163\t          node-version: '22'\n164\t          cache: npm\n165\t\n166\t      - name: Install (no build)\n167\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n168\t\n169\t      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n170\t      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n171\t      - name: Audit (high and above)\n172\t        run: npm run check:audit\n173\t\n174\t      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n175\t      # repository credentials.\n176\t      - name: Action pins\n177\t        run: npm run check:action-pins\n178\t\n179\t  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n180\t  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n181\t  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n182\t  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n183\t  smoke:\n184\t    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n185\t    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n186\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n187\t    steps:\n188\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n189\t        with:\n190\t          persist-credentials: false\n191\t\n192\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n193\t        with:\n194\t          node-version: '22'\n195\t          cache: npm\n196\t\n197\t      - name: Install (no build)\n198\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n199\t\n200\t      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n201\t      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n202\t      - name: Build\n203\t        run: npm run build\n204\t\n205\t      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n206\t      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n207\t      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n208\t      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n209\t        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n210\t\n211\t      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n212\t        run: npm run smoke -- full\n213\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a5261796-ee91-4f64-97bb-e389bc300266","uuid":"d9d2c2ac-a0d5-40cb-bd7e-8f732d119546","timestamp":"2026-11-06T04:23:17.568Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/79d6e7933ca1/workspace/target/.github/workflows/ci.yml","content":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n      # passing check should look like.\n      #\n      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n      - name: Spec citations name their test\n        run: npm run spec:names\n\n      - name: Spec link placement\n        run: npm run check:spec-links\n\n      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n      # and never gates.\n      - name: Spec status\n        run: npm run check:spec-status\n\n      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The\n      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.\n      - name: Changelog entry\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')\n        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes\n        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step\n        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private\n        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.\n        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh \"origin/${{ github.base_ref }}\"\n\n  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain\n  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as\n  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n  build-chain:\n    name: Build chain\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n      - name: Audit (high and above)\n        run: npm run check:audit\n\n      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n      # repository credentials.\n      - name: Action pins\n        run: npm run check:action-pins\n\n  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n  smoke:\n    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n\n      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n        run: npm run smoke -- full\n","numLines":213,"startLine":1,"totalLines":213}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_2a20e4c274274b7f85a2941b","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

type {\n  SchemaType,\n  Content,\n  GenerateContentRequest,\n  GenerateContentResponse,\n  FunctionCallPart,\n  FunctionDeclarationSchema,\n  Part,\n} from '@google-cloud/vertexai';\nimport {AIError} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {\n  AIProvider,\n  Message,\n  MessageChunk,\n  SendMessageParams,\n  StructuredOutputParams,\n  ResponseSchema,\n  UsageMetadata,\n} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\nimport {requireOptionalPeer} from '../requireOptionalPeer.js';\n\nexport interface VertexConfig {\n  type: 'vertex';\n  projectId: string;\n  location: string;\n  modelId: string;\n  maxTokens?: number;\n  googleAuthOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\nexport function createVertexProvider(config: VertexConfig): AIProvider {\n  const {VertexAI} = requireOptionalPeer<typeof import('@google-cloud/vertexai')>('@google-cloud/vertexai');\n  const vertexAI = new VertexAI({\n    project: config.projectId,\n    location: config.location,\n    googleAuthOptions: config.googleAuthOptions,\n  });\n\n  const model = vertexAI.getGenerativeModel({\n    model: config.modelId,\n    generationConfig: {maxOutputTokens: config.maxTokens},\n  });\n\n  return {\n    async *sendMessage(params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      log.info('vertex', 'sending message', {\n        modelId: config.modelId,\n        messageCount: params.messages.length,\n        hasTools: !!params.tools,\n      });\n\n      try {\n        const request = buildRequest(params);\n        if (params.maxTokens) {\n          request.generationConfig = {maxOutputTokens: params.maxTokens};\n        }\n\n        const streamResult = await model.generateContentStream(request);\n\n        for await (const chunk of streamResult.stream) {\n          const candidate = chunk.candidates?.[0];\n          if (!candidate?.content?.parts) continue;\n\n          yield* partChunks(candidate.content.parts);\n\n          const finishReason = candidate.finishReason;\n          if (finishReason) {\n            const stopReason =\n              finishReason === 'STOP'\n                ? 'end_turn'\n                : finishReason === 'MAX_TOKENS'\n                  ? 'max_tokens'\n                  : finishReason.toLowerCase();\n            yield {type: 'stop', stopReason, usage: extractUsage(chunk)};\n          }\n        }\n      } catch (error) {\n        log.error('vertex', 'stream error', {error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown'});\n        throw mapVertexError(error);\n      }\n    },\n\n    async generateStructured<T>(params: StructuredOutputParams<T>): Promise<T> {\n      log.info('vertex', 'generating structured output', {\n        modelId: config.modelId,\n        messageCount: params.messages.length,\n      });\n\n      try {\n        const structuredModel = vertexAI.getGenerativeModel({\n          model: config.modelId,\n          generationConfig: {\n            maxOutputTokens: params.maxTokens ?? config.maxTokens,\n            responseMimeType: 'application/json',\n            responseSchema: mapResponseSchema(params.responseSchema),\n          },\n        });\n\n        const request: GenerateContentRequest = {\n          contents: params.messages.map(mapMessage),\n          systemInstruction: {role: 'user', parts: [{text: params.systemPrompt}]},\n        };\n\n        const result = await structuredModel.generateContent(request);\n        const text = extractText(result.response);\n\n        return JSON.parse(text) as T;\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof SyntaxError) {\n          throw new AIError('Failed to parse structured response as JSON', 'PARSE_ERROR');\n        }\n        log.error('vertex', 'structured output error', {error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown'});\n        throw mapVertexError(error);\n      }\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// A part can carry text and a function call at once, so it maps to 0, 1 or 2 chunks.\nfunction* partChunks(parts: Part[]): Generator<MessageChunk> {\n  for (const part of parts) {\n    if ('text' in part && part.text) {\n      yield {type: 'text', text: part.text};\n    }\n\n    if ('functionCall' in part) {\n      const fc = (part as FunctionCallPart).functionCall;\n      yield {\n        type: 'tool_use',\n        toolCall: {\n          id: fc.name,\n          name: fc.name,\n          input: (fc.args ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>,\n        },\n      };\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction buildRequest(params: SendMessageParams): GenerateContentRequest {\n  const request: GenerateContentRequest = {\n    contents: params.messages.map(mapMessage),\n    systemInstruction: {role: 'user', parts: [{text: params.systemPrompt}]},\n  };\n\n  if (params.tools?.length) {\n    request.tools = [\n      {\n        functionDeclarations: params.tools.map(t => ({\n          name: t.name,\n          description: t.description,\n          parameters: t.inputSchema as unknown as FunctionDeclarationSchema,\n        })),\n      },\n    ];\n  }\n\n  return request;\n}\n\nfunction mapMessage(m: Message): Content {\n  if (typeof m.content === 'string') {\n    return {role: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'model' : 'user', parts: [{text: m.content}]};\n  }\n\n  const parts = m.content.map(block => {\n    if (block.type === 'tool_use') {\n      return {\n        functionCall: {\n          name: block.name,\n          args: block.input,\n        },\n      };\n    }\n    return {\n      functionResponse: {\n        name: block.toolUseId,\n        response: {result: block.content},\n      },\n    };\n  });\n\n  return {role: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'model' : 'user', parts};\n}\n\nfunction extractUsage(response: GenerateContentResponse): UsageMetadata | undefined {\n  const usage = response.usageMetadata;\n  if (!usage) return undefined;\n  return {\n    inputTokens: usage.promptTokenCount ?? 0,\n    outputTokens: usage.candidatesTokenCount ?? 0,\n    totalTokens: usage.totalTokenCount ?? 0,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction mapVertexError(error: unknown): AIError {\n  if (error instanceof AIError) return error;\n  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown Vertex AI error';\n  if (message.includes('429') || message.includes('RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED')) {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line re-lint/no-flag-params -- AIError's retryable flag; see adrs/ADR-006-lint-suppressions.md\n    return new AIError(message, 'RATE_LIMITED', true);\n  }\n  if (message.includes('401') || message.includes('403') || message.includes('PERMISSION_DENIED')) {\n    return new AIError(message, 'AUTH_ERROR');\n  }\n  return new AIError(message, 'PROVIDER_ERROR');\n}\n\nfunction mapResponseSchema(schema: ResponseSchema): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const mapped: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    type: schema.type.toUpperCase() as SchemaType,\n  };\n\n  if (schema.description) mapped.description = schema.description;\n  if (schema.enum) mapped.enum = schema.enum;\n\n  if (schema.properties) {\n    mapped.properties = Object.fromEntries(\n      Object.entries(schema.properties).map(([key, value]) => [key, mapResponseSchema(value)])\n    );\n  }\n  if (schema.required) mapped.required = schema.required;\n  if (schema.items) mapped.items = mapResponseSchema(schema.items);\n\n  return mapped;\n}\n\nfunction extractText(response: GenerateContentResponse): string {\n  const candidate = response.candidates?.[0];\n  const parts = candidate?.content?.parts;\n  if (!parts) return '';\n  const texts = parts.filter((p): p is {text: string} => 'text' in p && typeof p.text === 'string').map(p => p.text);\n  return texts.join('');\n}\n","numLines":235,"startLine":1,"totalLines":235}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_22794e9557a84338a50ae0ea","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_29e843334b3b49fc9288737e","type":"tool_result","content":"15:// One expect per test needs the rejection as a value rather than a matcher.\n281:      await expect(orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('hello'))).rejects.toThrow('boom');\n436:  it('forwards the client messages a tool returned as one tool_result chunk', async () => {\n446:    expect(chunks).toContainEqual({type: 'tool_result', clientMessages: [forwarded]});\n461:      type: 'tool_result',\n523:  it('feeds a schema rejection to the provider as a tool_result and resolves the turn instead of rejecting', async () => {\n558:      rejectionVisibleToProvider: JSON.stringify(secondRoundMessages).includes('location'),\n559:    }).toEqual({reply: 'all done', rejectionVisibleToProvider: true});\n# Tool Input Validation\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\nEvery tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n\n## Validation at execute time\n\n- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16), [validated by: rejects missing required input without calling the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L21)).\n- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: passes valid input with an unlisted extra property through to the executor unchanged, exactly once](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L94)).\n- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake ([validated by: throws Unknown tool for a name that was never registered](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L110)).\n\n## Schema compilation and caching\n\n- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).\n- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: compiles a static tool schema once at registration and reuses it across calls](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L42)).\n- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: validates a function-valued source against the schema current at each call](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L59)).\n\n## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n\n- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112), [validated by: feeds a schema rejection to the provider as a tool_result and resolves the turn instead of rejecting](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L523)).","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a5261796-ee91-4f64-97bb-e389bc300266","uuid":"6a3b377b-6ff2-40de-8ed8-c26f62b02daa","timestamp":"2026-11-06T04:34:45.340Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"15://
